abstract: Thyroid cancer （TC） is one of the most common endocrine malignancies with high incidence and heterogeneity.Its diagnosis mainly relies on ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy，while it still fails to give a definitive diagnosis in 15%-30% of lesions，leading to a large number of unnecessary repeat biopsies and surgical procedures.Metabolomics，as a newly developed discipline，plays a role in the early diagnosis，treatment，and prognosis of TC by detecting differential metabolites in a variety of biological samples，such as tissue and blood，and researching the differential expression of metabolic pathways in TC.This review summarizes the research progress of metabolomics in the last 5 years，aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the screening of diagnostic biomarkers and exploring potential therapeutic targets for TC.
